title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues concerning Standardizing Sentencing Procedures (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court   Supreme People's Procuratorate

Ministry of Public Security   Ministry of State Security   Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues concerning Standardizing Sentencing Procedures (for Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2010] No. 35

To: the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), State Security Departments (Bureaus), and Justice Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army and the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, the Public Security Bureau, the State Security Bureau, and the Justice Bureau:

In order to further standardize sentencing procedures and promote openness and impartiality in sentencing activities, and in accordance with the overall plan of the Central Committee on deepening judicial system and working mechanism reform, on the basis of in-depth investigation, research, and extensive solicitation of opinions from all sides, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice have jointly formulated the Opinions on Several Issues concerning Standardizing Sentencing Procedures (for Trial Implementation). The Opinions are hereby issued for your conscientious implementation. Any issues arising during implementation and problems encountered shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice respectively.

September 13, 2010

Opinions on Several Issues concerning Standardizing Sentencing Procedures (for Trial Implementation)

To further standardize sentencing activities and promote openness and impartiality in sentencing, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law and judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual circumstances of criminal judicial work.

Article 1 When a People's Court hears a criminal case, it shall ensure the relative independence of the sentencing activities.

Article 2 Investigative organs and People's Procuratorates shall, in accordance with statutory procedures, collect various types of evidence capable of proving the severity of the crime of a criminal suspect or defendant, as well as other evidence relevant to sentencing.

For cases where a People's Procuratorate initiates a public prosecution, the transfer of sentencing evidence materials shall be carried out in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 3 For public prosecution cases, the People's Procuratorate may propose a sentencing recommendation. Sentencing recommendations shall generally have a certain range.

When a People's Procuratorate proposes a sentencing recommendation, it shall generally prepare a sentencing recommendation letter and submit it together with the indictment to the People's Court; depending on the specific circumstances of the case, the People's Procuratorate may also propose a sentencing recommendation within the written opinion of public prosecution. For cases subject to summary procedure where the People's Procuratorate does not send a representative to appear in court, a sentencing recommendation letter shall be prepared and submitted together with the indictment to the People's Court.

A sentencing recommendation letter shall generally state the type of punishment, the range of punishment, the method of execution of the punishment that the People's Procuratorate recommends to be imposed on the defendant, as well as the reasons and basis therefor.

Article 4 During the litigation process, the parties, defenders, and agents ad litem may present sentencing opinions and state the reasons therefor.

Article 5 If the People's Procuratorate proposes a sentencing recommendation in the form of a sentencing recommendation letter, the People's Court shall serve the sentencing recommendation letter together with the copy of the indictment to the defendant.

Article 6 For public prosecution cases, especially cases where the defendant does not plead guilty or disputes the sentencing recommendation, and where the defendant, due to financial difficulties or other reasons, does not have a defender, the People's Court may assign a lawyer through a legal aid institution to provide defense for the defendant.

Article 7 For cases tried under summary procedure, after confirming that the defendant has no objection to the facts and charges of the crime alleged in the indictment, voluntarily pleads guilty, and is aware of the legal consequences of pleading guilty, the court trial may proceed directly focusing on sentencing issues.

Article 8 For cases where the defendant pleads guilty and is tried under ordinary procedure, after confirming that the defendant understands the facts and charges of the crime alleged in the indictment, voluntarily pleads guilty, and is aware of the legal consequences of pleading guilty, the court trial shall mainly focus on sentencing and other disputed issues.

Article 9 For cases where the defendant does not plead guilty or the defender makes a not-guilty defense, during the stage of court investigation, the relevant sentencing facts shall be ascertained. During the stage of court debate, the judicial personnel shall guide the prosecution and defense to first debate the issue of conviction. After the conclusion of the conviction debate, the judicial personnel shall inform the prosecution and defense that they may debate around sentencing issues, present sentencing recommendations or opinions, and state the reasons and basis therefor.

Article 10 During the court investigation, the People's Court shall ascertain the statutory or discretionary sentencing circumstances that are applicable to the defendant under a specific statutory range of punishment, as well as other circumstances warranting heavier punishment, lighter punishment, mitigation of punishment, or exemption from punishment.

Article 11 If a People's Court, People's Procuratorate, investigative organ, or defender commissions a relevant party to prepare a social investigation report involving a minor, such report shall be read out in court and subject to cross-examination.

Article 12 During court proceedings, if the judicial personnel have doubts about the sentencing evidence, they may adjourn the session to investigate and verify the evidence, and if necessary, may also require the People's Procuratorate to conduct supplementary investigation and verification. The People's Procuratorate shall conduct supplementary investigation and verification of the relevant evidence, and if necessary, may require the investigative organ to provide assistance.

Article 13 If a party, defender, or agent ad litem applies to the People's Court to obtain sentencing evidence materials collected during investigation or review of prosecution, and the People's Court deems it truly necessary, it shall obtain such evidence in accordance with the law. If the People's Court considers it unnecessary to obtain the relevant sentencing evidence materials, it shall state the reasons therefor.

Article 14 Sentencing debate activities shall be conducted in the following order:

(1) The public prosecutor or private prosecutor and his or her agent ad litem present sentencing recommendations or opinions;

(2) The victim (or the plaintiff in a collateral civil action) and his or her agent ad litem present sentencing opinions;

(3) The defendant and his or her defender present a defense and sentencing opinions.

Article 15 During the court debate, if new sentencing facts emerge that require further investigation, the court investigation shall be resumed, and the court debate shall continue after the facts are clarified.

Article 16 The criminal judgment documents of the People's Court shall state the reasons for sentencing. The reasons for sentencing shall mainly include:

(1) The sentencing facts that have been ascertained and their effect on sentencing;

(2) The reasons for whether to adopt the sentencing recommendations or opinions presented by the public prosecutor, parties, defenders, and agents ad litem;

(3) The People's Court's reasons and legal basis for sentencing.

Article 17 For sentencing activities in second instance or retrial cases that are tried with a hearing, they shall be conducted in accordance with relevant legal provisions. Where the law has no provisions, these Opinions shall be referred to.

For second instance or retrial cases that are tried without a hearing, when the judicial personnel review the case files, interrogate the defendant, and hear the opinions of other parties, defenders, and agents ad litem, they shall pay attention to examining the sentencing facts and evidence.

Article 18 These Opinions shall be implemented on a trial basis as of October 1, 2010.
